verifications.claim: NASA's Artemis II mission successfully lifted off on April 1, 2026.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'Artemis II lifted off at 6:35 p.m. EDT.' (with post-liftoff updates confirming success); R7: 'lifted off from Kennedy Space Center in Florida at 6:35 p.m. ET.'
verifications.reasoning: Multiple sources directly confirm successful liftoff on April 1, 2026.

verifications.claim: NASA's Artemis II mission lifted off at 6:35 p.m. EDT (2235 UTC).
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'Artemis II lifted off at 6:35 p.m. EDT.'; R6: 'Artemis II has officially lifted off at 6:35 p.m. EDT'; R7: 'lifted off... at 6:35 p.m. ET.'
verifications.reasoning: Sources explicitly state liftoff at 6:35 p.m. EDT; UTC equivalent matches (2235 UTC = 6:35 p.m. EDT).

verifications.claim: NASA's Artemis II mission lifted off from Launch Pad 39B at the Kennedy Space Center in Florida.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'launching from the Kennedy Space Center in Florida, using the historic Launch Complex 39B.'; R4: 'Launch Pad 39B at NASA's Kennedy Space Center near Cape Canaveral, Florida.'
verifications.reasoning: Direct confirmation of exact launch site in multiple sources.

verifications.claim: Artemis II has a four-person crew.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'the four astronauts'; R2: 'four astronauts'; R4: 'four astronauts'; R6: 'four astronauts'; R7: 'four astronauts'.
verifications.reasoning: All relevant sources consistently describe a four-person crew.

verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R2: 'The 10-day mission around the moon'; R4: '10-day mission'; R5: '10 days'; R6: '10-day journey'; R7: '10-day mission'.
verifications.reasoning: Multiple sources directly call it a 10-day mission; R1 notes 'nine and a half days' but others round to 10 consistently.

verifications.claim: Artemis II marks the first crewed lunar flight since 1972.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'first piloted moonshot since the end of the Apollo program 53 years ago'; 'higher than any astronauts have flown since the final Apollo moon mission in 1972.'; R2: 'more than 50 years since we've headed toward the moon'.
verifications.reasoning: Sources explicitly state it is the first crewed mission to the moon since Apollo 17 in 1972.

verifications.claim: Live coverage of the Artemis II mission was provided by NASA and major news outlets.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: Live blog with timestamps; R2: 'how to watch live stream'; R6: 'Live Updates from Fox News Digital'; R7: 'live blog'.
verifications.reasoning: Sources are themselves live coverage from NASA and outlets like CBS, Florida Today, Fox, NBC.

verifications.claim: Artemis II is a crewed circumlunar mission.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'loop around it, getting an unprecedented view of the far side of the moon'; R2: 'fly around the Earth before going around the moon'; R5: 'journey around the moon'.
verifications.reasoning: Sources describe it as crewed mission flying around the moon (circum lunar trajectory).

verifications.claim: The crew of Artemis II is Reid Wiseman, Victor Glover, Christina Koch, Jeremy Hansen
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'commander Reid Wiseman, pilot Victor Glover, mission specialist Christina Koch and Canadian astronaut Jeremy Hansen'; R2: 'Reid Wiseman, commander; Victor Glover, pilot; Christina Koch, mission specialist; Jeremy Hansen, mission specialist'.
verifications.reasoning: Exact crew names listed in multiple sources, matching order and roles.
